newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery becoming more solid--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery becoming more solid--BOJ.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery is becoming more solid, and the recovery will continue after a temporary slowdown caused by a rise in the sales tax this month, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Monday.

Matsushita said the BOJ's basic stance regarding currency movements was reflected in an agreement of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations that excessive fluctuations in currency rates were not desirable.
He also said the G7 agreement stipulated that currency rates should reflect economic fundamentals.

"I want to refrain from making comments on specific currency levels, but recent currency movements are somewhat too rapid and we will keep watch on the trend," he said in a speech to a group of business leaders.

Matsushita said the central bank had since last autumn maintained the view that the economic recovery was becoming He added that the recovery was due to a cyclical mechanism in which a rise in production led to a recovery in capital spending and an improvement in employment, through a rise in corporate earnings.

Referring to the impact of this month's rise in the sales tax to five percent from three percent, he said the effects of various fiscal measures would be most strongly felt during the summer, and it was inevitable that the economy would slow down temporarily.
But he said the trend of the economic recovery itself was likely to continue after this temporary slowdown, due to the strengthening of the cyclical mechanism.

Matsushita said the BOJ would continue to carefully watch price movements. He said the trend of a fall in prices had come to a halt since the end of last year due to an improvement in domestic demand and a rise in import prices.

"Although upward pressure on prices from a rise in import prices is unlikely to strengthen further, we will continue to watch future price movements, taking into account the effects of a weak yen," he said.
Matsushita said taking into account prices and the conditions of the economy, the BOJ would continue to conduct monetary policy putting emphasis on making the economic recovery more solid.
"For the time being, in carrying out our monetary policy we will continue to put emphasis on strengthening the basis of the economic recovery."
Matsushita also said major Japanese banks are likely to complete disposal of problem loans within the next one or two years.
Commenting on an announcement on April 1 of a restructuring plan of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), Matsushita said he expects the bank to succeed in restructuring its business.

"This, along with a merger of two Hokkaido banks, is expected dispel uncertainties over Japan's financial system and to make a great contribution to restoring credibility in the financial system both at home and abroad," he said.
Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and the regional Hokkaido Bank announced on April 1 that they would merge by April next year with the aim of becoming a "super-regional" bank.
